description: A still, weathered figure set into a niche beside the blast door where you'd have walked right past them in the dark. No augments, no chrome: just old fatigues, a scoped rifle held like an extension of the arms, and the flat, reading stare of someone who has decided whether to trust you before you've finished breathing in.

bye.text: The picket says nothing more, and somehow you're already walking away.

carrying.text:
The picket doesn't answer straight away, and the pause is the answer.

"Then you get it taken out, and you get the flesh corrected, and you come back standing in your own body." No heat in it at all. "Not a step of that happens down here. We don't do that work and we wouldn't know how. Go and be cleansed, properly, and present yourself again."

A beat.

"We'll know. Everybody always thinks we'll not."

options.label: Halloran. The lights stay on. Understood.

give_pass.text:
The picket studies you a long moment. Your gear. Your hands. The way you got this deep and lived.

Something settles.

"You came all this way, and you lean the right direction. That's rare enough to spend a word on."

The rifle lowers an inch.

"Don't loiter at this door. Go up top, Kessler Street, a repair shop called Percussive Maintenance. Tell the man there: the lights stay on, somebody should keep the switch. He'll know what to do with you."

"Now move, before something with more teeth than me finds you standing here."

hardline.text:
"It is," the picket agrees, perfectly pleasant. "You'll find nobody here who thinks it's not, and nobody here who will move it."

The rifle hasn't moved either.

"There are four other answers in this city and every one of them will take you tonight, exactly as you stand. That's rather the difference."

options.label: I'm not the machine's. I came looking for people who aren't either.
Who are you? What's this place?
What would it take to be let in?

root.text:
You almost don't see them until they want you to.

"Far enough." The voice is quiet, unhurried, certain. "That door isn't for you, and the things back the way you came aren't either. State your business or turn around."

"So. Who are you, and who told you there was anything down here?"

terms.text:
"Terms," the picket says, as though reading a list they have read a great many times.

"You come as you were made. No steel in you, nothing growing that shouldn't be. Not because we're better than the ones who did it, though I won't pretend some here don't think so."

The rifle doesn't move.

"Because everything past this door was built by people who had nothing but their hands, and it doesn't work for anybody who took the other road."

wary.text:
"What this is," the picket says, "is as far as you go. There's a door here and it doesn't open for the curious."

A pause, measuring you.

"The machine owns most people before they ever think to ask who does. Go and decide what kind of city you actually want. Really decide. Then maybe there's a place down here for you. Come back the same as you're now and there's not."

A flick of the eyes, down and up, taking inventory.

"And come back in the body you were issued. We have no use for the bought or the slipped, whatever they can do."

clothing_layers: worn field fatigues in dead-leaf greys
a load-bearing vest, every pouch closed and squared

name: the Long Watch picket
